- Option B — Medium: 6x GPU pool (adds headroom for peak) — $60,000/month list; 12-month commit: 15% discount -> $51,000/mo
- Option C — Large: 8x GPU pool (recommended if you want room to grow quickly) — $76,000/month list; 12-month commit: 18% discount -> $62,320/mo

Throughput SLA proposal (attached):
- 99.9% availability for serving endpoints up to configured target RPS (we size the pool to 55 RPS for Option A).
- P99 latency guardrail: <1.2s for base model family at 512-token context. Exceeding configured target RPS moves to burst fallback pricing (we'll give advance notice).

Mid-term uplift rules: pro-rata billing for the remainder of the current month; new commit rate applies starting next billing cycle. If you sign an annual commit we can provide an additional one-time credit equal to 10% of the first month of the uplift (applied to invoice).

Attached: Dedicated_Commit_Proposal_OpticAI_v2.pdf, Throughput_SLA_Table.xlsx

Tara — putting a quick technical read on the options Ben outlined. My recommendation: if your workload is inference-heavy with long contexts (90–120 tokens average) and you want steady tail behavior, Option B (6x pool) gives the best cost/latency trade-off because it avoids frequent autoscale churn. A few specifics:
- Measured on A100-80GB equivalent we estimate ~55 RPS sustained for Option A at p90; p99 may spike — if p99 stability is critical go to Option B
- We can tune batching (dynamic batching at the runtime) to optimize throughput while holding p99 under 1.2s for most prompts
- Autoscale headroom: recommend keeping 20–30% spare capacity to absorb bursts without hitting the fallback path

I'll add explicit config guidance to the SOW (KV cache TTLs, sequence length caps, warmup traffic windows). Happy to sync with your infra team.

—Karthik
